name: Village of Rye Brook
gaps: Verified against eCode360 Ch. 250 (RY1192) on 2026-11-25; no pending new laws affect Ch. 250
No distinct corner-lot street side yard in the schedule (accessory rule refers to 'corner lot side yard setbacks' without a number); corner_side_ft null
Minimum lot depth not set; lot width recorded from the 'horizontal circle diameter'
GFA formula gives less than 4,000 sf for lots under 21,780 sf (base + negative adjustment)
R-25/R-20 front yards rise to the neighbors' average setback where those are deeper (§§ 250-18.2H, 250-19G); not modelled
RA-1 has no FAR ('none') and is not in the § 250-37 coverage tables; R-35 (code district, not in county data) not added

wetlands.summary: Ch. 245: permit for regulated activities in wetlands, watercourses and the wetland/watercourse buffer, at least 100 ft from the wetland boundary or watercourse bank (more where DEC or the approval authority designates); small-scope work by administrative permit from the Village Engineer.

steep_slopes.summary: Ch. 213: steep slope work permit to disturb areas of 15%+ gradient covering at least 100 sf; classes 15-25% moderately steep, 25-35% very steep, 35%+ extremely steep.

trees.summary: Ch. 235: Tree Removal Permit to cut down any tree of 10 in. DBH or more on private improved property (§ 235-8); significant trees are 30 in.+ DBH.

stormwater.summary: Ch. 217: stormwater review for activities adding 400 sf or more of impervious surface; major land development at 20,000 sf of disturbance.

adu.summary: No accessory-apartment use; rear buildings may be lived in only by domestic employees (max 2 stories/30 ft, 30 ft from the main building) (§ 250-6E(5)(d)). In R2-F, pre-existing dwellings may be converted to more units at 750 sf per family (§ 250-25).

general.accessory_structures: Detached accessory buildings up to 1 story / 15 ft may sit in side or rear yards at least 5 ft from lot lines and 12 ft from the house; not in front or corner-side yards (§ 250-6B(1)(h)). Accessory building coverage 3.5-5% and decks 3.5-5% by district (§ 250-37B).
general.pools: Ch. 224: pool water's edge at least 15 ft from every property line; filters/heaters/pumps 10 ft from lot lines (or underground); not in a front yard; on a corner lot, a pool in the street-side yard needs the front setback on both streets; water area max 10% of the lot; 4 ft fence (§§ 224-7, 224-11).
general.notes: Porches may not project into required yards; eaves/sills up to 2 ft (§ 250-6B(1)).

R-25.name: R-25 One-Family Residential

max_building_coverage.note: Main building; plus accessory buildings 3.5% and decks 4% (§ 250-37B); second floor may not exceed the first-floor allowance

max_floor_area.note: Main building: 4,000 + (lot area - 21,780) x 0.11478421 (lots under 21,780 sf get less than 4,000). Gross floor area (§ 250-2) counts all floors incl. attached garages; basements/cellars excluded unless the finished ceiling is 5 ft+ above mean natural grade; unfinished half-story space under 7.5 ft excluded; areas 14 ft+ high count twice; enclosed porches count, open porches do not (§ 250-6B(1)(b)-(c)); attic or space over a garage 7 ft+ high counts

accessory.notes: Detached accessory building of 1 story / 15 ft max may sit in a side or rear yard, no nearer than 5 ft to a property line and 12 ft from the main building; front and corner-side setbacks still apply (§ 250-6B(1)(h))

R-25.notes: Lot width is the code's minimum 'horizontal circle diameter'. Front-yard impervious coverage max 20% (§ 250-37D). Front yard increases to the average of neighboring setbacks where those are deeper; corner lots compute a front yard for each street frontage. Height/setback ratio (inclined plane from the lot line, § 250-2): front 0.48, side 1.30. Usable open space 1,200 sf per dwelling unit.
